transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-30
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Patel (Redwood SE), Anika Verma (Redwood Product), Carlos Ruiz (HyperGrid Head Integrations), Priya Nair (HyperGrid Security), Tom Becker (HyperGrid PM), Elena Kors (HyperGrid Marketplace)

Summary:
Quick technical sync to align on co-engineering playbook for a joint marketplace listing and to surface security/licensing blockers. Discussed deployment patterns (VPC connector vs marketplace packaged helm), quantization/latency expectations, billing/licensing flows, and initial benchmarking plan. Agreed on deliverables and dates.

Topics covered:
- Goal: marketplace listing + joint refarch that HyperGrid can ship to enterprise customers with Redwood inference backing.
- Packaging options: helm operator vs pre-baked AMI/container image + marketplace listing constraints.
- Networking: VPC connectivity patterns, private endpoint, egress rules.
- Security: SOC2, KMS integration, audit logs, key rotation expectations.
- Performance: latency SLOs, batching, KV cache behavior.
- Licensing: billing flow in marketplace, metering, trial entitlements.
- Pilot plan: benchmarks, UAT, success criteria.

Action items (captured verbally in the call):
- Redwood to share playbook draft and sample manifests.
- SE to run benchmarks and provide 95th percentile latency numbers for 1k token workloads.
- HyperGrid to share compliance contacts and timeline for approvals.
- Marketplace owner to confirm listing gating criteria and lead times.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, appreciate it. i think we have about an hour, just want to run through the co-engineering playbook and make sure the marketplace constraints line up.
[00:06] Carlos Ruiz: yeah thanks maya. quick note, we pulled up the internal refarch doc, have a few questions about VPC flow and also, um, the licensing model you suggested in the one pager.
[00:12] Liam Patel: cool, i'm happy to jump into the network bits. just as background, Redwood's runtime supports both a VPC connector mode and a packaged deployment for marketplace images. we call them — uh — Redwood Private and Redwood Dedicated sometimes, but audio sucks so it might come out wrong on the record.
[00:24] Priya Nair: can you explain the difference for our security folks? VPC connector versus packaged? we need details about key management.
[00:30] Liam Patel: yep. VPC connector is basically customer-hosted network peering, your infra initiates outbound to Redwood control plane, or we can do a private link style. packaged deployment is if you want the inference runtime running inside your marketplace hosted environment — that one needs our operator and the KMS integration to be set up on your side.
[00:42] Tom Becker: is there a recommended for enterprise customers? like which gives better latency?
[00:46] Anika Verma: from product side, the tradeoff is predictable latency with Dedicated/pinned infra vs lowest onboarding friction with hosted API. but for marketplace where customers expect single-click install, the packaged operator often maps better. though you may see higher network hop latency if control plane remains outside.
[00:58] Carlos Ruiz: okay that partly answers it. i'm worried about audit logs — our customers ask for retention and we have to surface them in the marketplace contract. what does redwood provide?
[01:05] Liam Patel: we generate per-request logs with token-level costing in the console, you can export aggregated telemetry and raw traces to your SIEM. there are slight naming mismatches in the api, the field is sometimes listed as "token_cost_est" in older docs.
[01:18] Priya Nair: uh, is encryption at rest covered by the packaged operator or we need to wire our KMS? we need customer-controlled keys.
[01:24] Maya Chen: customers can bring their own KMS for Private and for packaged on-prem operator. for hosted listing there is a contract option to use a customer-managed KMS via our integration (requires some entitle/contract changes).
[01:34] Elena Kors: marketplace teams typically want an AMI or container that passes their security scan. do you have a recommended image baseline?
[01:41] Liam Patel: yes, we have hardened images we can share. they are based on distroless builds but we do need to add a thin operator and systemd bits for lifecycle. i'll attach the manifest and the SBOM — well, i'll attach in the doc after the call.
[01:53] Carlos Ruiz: SBOM is important. also, for the billing, how does metering work if we list through HyperGrid marketplace? is it meter by token, by request, or seat?
[02:00] Maya Chen: primary is per-token for hosted API; for Marketplace the common pattern is to surface a metered billing connector with monthly reconciliation. we also support reserved capacity contracts booked through our sales channel if a customer wants predictable commit.
[02:12] Tom Becker: does that mean the marketplace takes a cut and we invoice separately? need to confirm the money flow.
[02:16] Elena Kors: marketplace usually takes platform fees, yes. we can do pass-through billing or redwood direct billing with a reseller agreement. that will impact how licenses show up.
[02:24] Priya Nair: circling back to compliance — SOC2 report, do you have an excerpt we can share with our legal/compliance?
[02:30] Maya Chen: yes, i'll share our SOC2 + high-level controls doc. for deeper review we can do an NDA and share the full report.
[02:36] Priya Nair: okay please do that.
[02:38] [pause, typing noises]
[02:42] Liam Patel: on performance: we should define a baseline test. proposal: 1k token gen workload with 8 concurrent streams for 10 minutes, measure p50/p95/p99 latencies, and token cost. we can run on HyperGrid staging if you provide equivalent g4dn/rtx instance profile.
[02:55] Carlos Ruiz: sounds good, we'll spin up staging. what's the expected quantization impact? customers want good quality first.
[03:02] Anika Verma: we recommend starting with fp16/8-bit quantized models for cost, but we tie quality regression tests to your prompt suite. Redwood Optimize can run eval suites to detect regressions automatically.
[03:12] Tom Becker: can that be in the pipeline? we'd like to have automated evals in CI.
[03:15] Liam Patel: yes, there's a small agent you add to CI that runs a small eval harness against a pinned model commit. it reports back diffs. sometimes the labels come out as "model drift" but it's basically quality delta.
[03:26] Carlos Ruiz: okay, on the embedding side — not the main thing for marketplace but we do want to know storage sizing for KV caches.
[03:31] Liam Patel: KV cache memory is proportional to active context. we can provide recommended autoscaler settings. for example, for 8k context with 500 concurrent users, you'll need X memory per GPU — i will get exact numbers into the playbook.
[03:44] Priya Nair: any known issues with our cloud provider? we're on Nebula Cloud — i've seen in past docs some incompatibilities with private links.
[03:50] Maya Chen: we have a few customers on Nebula; there were quirks around service IP ranges and the private link handshake timing out if firewall stateful inspection was enabled. we'll document the firewall rules and retry window.
[04:01] Elena Kors: on marketplace listing gating: we need a packaging artifact, SBOM, security questionnaire, and a contract that includes data handling terms. typical lead time is 3 to 6 weeks after you submit everything.
[04:12] Maya Chen: understood. given that, we'd like to scope a pilot: 2-week UAT, 4-week pilot with 3 enterprise customers. success criteria: p95 < 600ms for 512-token prompts, no S3-level data leakage, and acceptance of contract terms by legal.
[04:25] Carlos Ruiz: p95 < 600ms — that's tight but maybe achievable if we tune batching. what if we hit 800ms?
[04:30] Anika Verma: we can propose fallback policies: route to faster model variants during spikes, use cache warmers for prefix-heavy workloads. also suggest a canary rollout to 10% of traffic first.
[04:40] Tom Becker: licensing question again: for the pilot, can we do trial credits that reduce to metered billing after 30 days?
[04:45] Maya Chen: yes, a trial entitlement can be provisioned; typically we define a credit bucket and an expiration. that will need to be reflected in the marketplace offer metadata.
[04:53] Priya Nair: about KMS: we require hardware-backed key store or HSM. supported?
[04:58] Liam Patel: we integrate with most major KMS offering HSM-backed keys. for packaged operator, you can connect to your own KMS endpoints. small caveat: rotation windows need to be coordinated, we have a key-rolling window that must be observed.
[05:09] Carlos Ruiz: noted. who will be the point of contact for security artifacts?
[05:13] Priya Nair: i'll own that from HyperGrid side, i'll collect the checklist.
[05:16] Maya Chen: perfect. i'll also copy our compliance lead in the follow-up.
[05:19] [short laughter]
[05:22] Elena Kors: oh also, marketplace marketing — we want a joint solution brief and a 1-pager for the launch. who does that?
[05:27] Anika Verma: product marketing usually drafts the co-branded brief. we can provide a technical diagram, 2 customer use case bullets, and a short ops checklist for onboarding.
[05:36] Maya Chen: ok action items recap: we'll produce the playbook, manifests, SBOM, and sample operator image. hypergrid provides staging access and compliance contact. se runs benchmarks. marketplace confirms listing timeline.
[05:46] Tom Becker: timeline wise, if we get artifacts by week of July 7, earliest listing could be end of July / early august?
[05:52] Elena Kors: more like early august if there are no blockers; otherwise mid-august.
[05:55] Carlos Ruiz: quick technical nit: when you say "operator", will we need cluster-admin privileges? that's a no-go for some of our customers.
[06:01] Liam Patel: good question. the operator requires elevated permissions for node lifecycle ops only. we can offer a limited-perm manifest that avoids cluster-admin by using sidecars and CRDs with reduced RBAC; there are tradeoffs in auto-scaling features though.
[06:13] Priya Nair: that's important. we'll need that limited-perm manifest for security review.
[06:17] Maya Chen: we'll add that to the playbook.
[06:20] [long pause, writing]
[06:35] Maya Chen: any other risks? i'm thinking of integration points — billing reconciliation, KMS rotation, and model version pinning.
[06:42] Carlos Ruiz: model pinning — if you push a new model we need the ability to opt-out until we've validated.
[06:47] Anika Verma: absolutely, rollout policies support pin-by-tenant and canary groups. we'll include a step-by-step for rollback.
[06:53] Tom Becker: one more: can you provide a small checklist for enterprise acceptance testing? network, perf, security checks?
[06:58] Liam Patel: yes, we'll include an acceptance checklist in the playbook. example items: network ranges open, KMS reachable, initial benchmark p95 within threshold, SBOM scanned, and legal T&Cs accepted.
[07:10] Maya Chen: cool. ok let's lock the due dates: playbook to HyperGrid by 2027-07-07, benchmarks by 2027-07-09, SOC2 excerpts by 2027-07-05, marketplace timeline confirmation by 2027-07-12.
[07:22] Carlos Ruiz: sounds good. thanks all. we'll follow up with calendar invites for the pilot planning meeting.
[07:27] Maya Chen: thank you. talk soon. bye.
[07:30] [meeting end]

Notes on transcript quality: some proper nouns may be misrecognized (e.g., "Redwood Dedicated" sometimes transcribed as "Redwood Dedicate"). timestamps are approximate and reflect Fireflies-style timestamping every ~15-90 seconds. Links referenced: playbook draft (link to be sent), SBOM artifact (link to be sent), SOC2 excerpt (NDA gating).
